newsitem.title: JAPAN: Credit union body to take over Sanpuku business.
newsitem.headline: Credit union body to take over Sanpuku business.

text.p: All assets and business of financially troubled Sanpuku Shinyo Kumiai will be taken over by the Resolution and Collection Bank Ltd (RCB), Osaka prefectural governor Isamu Yamada said in a statement.
The small Osaka-based credit union will return deposits excluding those over 100 million yen, he said.
Earlier, the Osaka prefectural government said it had ordered a partial suspension of the business of the credit union.
The RCB is a body set up to take over and wind up failed credit unions.
The RCB was set up in September to handle the bankruptcies of credit unions which have happened over the past two years and to deal with possible future failures of such financial institutions.
Credit unions are small financial institutions which take deposits and lend mainly to members.

Yamada said the Osaka government will make special loans to small and medium-sized companies in the region, if necessary, to prevent them from going bankrupt in reaction to the credit union's failure.
The credit union's assets totalled 33.9 billion yen.
Of the total, non-performing assets stood at 18.9 billion and 7.7 billion yen were unrecoverable, according to data provided by the Osaka prefectural government.
